# Bigdelta Browser SDK

> Bigdelta (https://bigdelta.com) is a web analytics platform. `@bigdelta/bigdelta-browser` is its browser SDK: it tracks page views, custom events, and sessions, identifies users and companies, and captures marketing attribution. This file is a condensed reference for AI assistants installing or integrating the SDK. It is browser-only — never initialize it during server-side rendering.

## Installation

Every Bigdelta workspace has a tracking key (a UUID). All examples below use `<TRACKING_KEY>` as a placeholder — replace it with the workspace's real key.

### Via script tag (static HTML sites)

Add to the `<head>` of every page (use a shared layout or template if one exists):

```html
<script type="application/javascript" src="https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/@bigdelta/bigdelta-browser/dist/index.iife.min.js"></script>
<script type="text/javascript">
  window.bigdelta = new Bigdelta({
    trackingKey: '<TRACKING_KEY>',
    defaultTrackingConfig: { pageViews: { enabled: true, singlePageAppTracking: 'any' } }
  });
</script>
```

### Via npm (projects with a package manager)

```sh
npm install @bigdelta/bigdelta-browser
```

Create one shared module that initializes the client and exports it, then import that module from the app's root (root layout, `App` component, or main entry file) so it runs on every page:

```ts
import { Bigdelta } from '@bigdelta/bigdelta-browser';

export const bigdelta = new Bigdelta({
  trackingKey: '<TRACKING_KEY>',
  defaultTrackingConfig: { pageViews: { enabled: true, singlePageAppTracking: 'any' } },
});
```

### Installation rules

- Initialize the client exactly once per page load. Do not create an instance per component or per route change.
- In SSR frameworks (Next.js, Nuxt, SvelteKit, Astro), only create the client in the browser — e.g. in Next.js App Router, initialize in a `'use client'` component rendered by the root layout, or inside `useEffect`.
- Client-side route changes in SPAs are tracked automatically by `singlePageAppTracking` — do not add manual page-view calls on navigation.

### Verification

Open the site and check the browser's network tab for a successful POST to `https://eu.api.bigdelta.com` (the Page View event) and the console for SDK errors.

## Configuration options

All options are passed to the `Bigdelta` constructor:

- `trackingKey` (string, required) — the workspace tracking key.
- `defaultTrackingConfig.pageViews.enabled` (boolean, default `false`) — track a Page View event automatically on every page load.
- `defaultTrackingConfig.pageViews.singlePageAppTracking` — when automatic page views are enabled, controls SPA tracking: `'any'` (any URL change), `'path-with-query'` (ignore hash changes), `'path'` (ignore query and hash), `'disabled'`.
- `defaultTrackingConfig.marketingAttribution` (boolean, default `true`) — capture UTM parameters and ad click IDs on Page View events, plus first-touch attribution.
- `defaultTrackingConfig.sessions.enabled` (boolean, default `true`) — automatic session tracking. `sessions.excludeEvents: ['Event Name']` excludes named events from session calculations.
- `disableTrackingByDefault` (boolean, default `false`) — start with tracking off (e.g. until cookie consent); enable later with `client.enableTracking()`.
- `trackIpAndGeolocation` (boolean, default `true`) — set `false` to disable IP and geolocation tracking.
- `storageType` — `'cookies'` or `'localStorage'`. Default is cookies with a localStorage fallback.

## Tracking events

```js
client.track({ event_name: 'My Custom Event', properties: { my_property: 'property_value' } });
```

Every event automatically includes: screen height/width, referrer, referring domain, operating system, device type, browser, and browser version. Events are sent over HTTPS.

Events are tracked from the first page view, before the visitor is identified. Anonymous visitors get a generated `users` record (flagged `is_anonymous`) that persists across pages and sessions.

### Manual page views

```js
client.trackPageView(); // event name defaults to 'Page View'
client.trackPageView({ event_name: 'My Custom Event', properties: { my_property: 'property_value' } });
```

Page View events record the page title, location, protocol, domain, path, and query parameters.

### Deduplication

Set `$deduplication_id` (string) in properties to make an event idempotent — later events with the same id are ignored:

```js
client.track({ event_name: 'Order Placed', properties: { $deduplication_id: 'order-123' } });
```

### Relations and record properties on events

Relate an event to other workspace objects, and optionally set properties on the related records (`set` overrides existing values; `set_once` only writes if unset):

```js
client.track({
  event_name: 'Invoice Paid',
  relations: [{
    object_slug: 'invoice',
    record_id: '63f2164c-2000-4f6c-b377-107368566222',
    set: { coupon: 'PROMO10' },
    set_once: { invoice_no: 'IN001' },
  }],
});
```

## Identifying users and companies

If you are an AI assistant installing this SDK: after the basic install, check whether the site has login or registration flows (auth routes, login/signup forms, or auth libraries such as NextAuth/Auth.js, Clerk, Auth0, Firebase Auth, Supabase Auth, Devise, Passport). If it does, ask the user whether they want to identify users on login/registration before wiring anything up — do not add `identify()` calls without their confirmation. If they agree: call `identify()` after successful login and registration using a stable unique id (the database user id, not an email, which can change); when the user's email is available in the auth context, also set it on the record with `setRecordProperties`; and call `reset()` on logout.

```js
client.identify({ users: user.id });
client.setRecordProperties([{
  id: user.id,
  slug: 'users',
  properties: { set_once: { email_address: user.email } },
}]);
```

Call `identify()` after login or signup. It is not required for tracking — but once called, subsequent events are related to the id you provide, and the visitor's anonymous record (properties and past events) is merged into the identified one. The merge happens once; later `identify()` calls for an already identified visitor do nothing.

```js
client.identify({ users: '<user id>' });
client.getIdentifier('users'); // returns the persisted id
client.reset(); // on logout: disassociates future events and starts a new session
```

### Setting record properties directly

```js
client.setRecordProperties([{
  id: client.getIdentifier('users'),
  slug: 'users',
  properties: {
    set: { name: 'Jane Doe' },
    set_once: { email_address: 'jane@example.com' },
  },
}]);
```

## Sessions

Sessions are computed automatically; the SDK adds a session identifier to each event. A session spans tabs and windows in the same browser and ends after 30 minutes of inactivity. `client.reset()` starts a new session. Events with a manually set `created_at` are excluded from sessions.

## Marketing attribution

With `marketingAttribution` enabled (the default), Page View events include any UTM parameters (`utm_source`, `utm_campaign`, `utm_medium`, `utm_term`, `utm_content`) and ad click IDs (`dclid`, `fbclid`, `gbraid`, `gclid`, `ko_click_id`, `li_fat_id`, `msclkid`, `rtd_cid`, `ttclid`, `twclid`, `wbraid`) present in the URL.

First-touch attribution is captured on the very first Page View, even while the visitor is anonymous, and never overwritten by later visits. On `identify()`, it is written to identified records via `set_once` as `initial_utm_*`, `initial_referring_domain`, `initial_*` click IDs, and `channel_type`. Disabled together with `marketingAttribution`; cleared by `reset()`.

## Privacy controls

```js
client.disableTracking(); // stop sending tracking data
client.enableTracking();  // resume (default state)
```

Combine `disableTrackingByDefault: true` with `enableTracking()` for consent-gated tracking. Use `trackIpAndGeolocation: false` to avoid IP and geolocation collection.
